name: Family Reunification

value.note: gross income over the previous 3 years (avg €25,000/yr), not including social welfare payments — effective 12 June 2026, up from €40,000

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the Irish citizen sponsor to show gross income of at least €75,000 over the previous 3 years (average €25,000/year, not including social welfare) — a MAJOR increase from €40,000, effective 12 June 2026. New accommodation/overcrowding-standard requirements also apply.
requirements.fix_path: Meet the income and accommodation requirements.

requirement_groups.name: EU Treaty Rights (family of EU/EEA/Swiss citizen)

requirements.blocker_text: This covers family of an EU/EEA/Swiss citizen exercising free movement rights in Ireland — governed by EU law, more generous than the standard non-EEA route, grants Stamp 4 directly with no income test of this kind.

requirement_groups.name: Category C non-EEA sponsor (e.g. GEP holders)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the non-EEA sponsor to complete a qualifying employment period plus meet income/accommodation tests — CSEP holders get immediate reunification instead of this waiting-period route.

evidence_required.document: Sponsor's income and accommodation evidence matching the applicable group

sources.title: Family reunification - Immigration Service Delivery (updated 27 Feb 2026)

notes: MAJOR LIVE POLICY EVENT confirmed and already in force: the Irish-citizen-sponsor income requirement JUMPED from €40,000 to €75,000 over 3 years, effective 12 June 2026 — a dramatic, dated, confirmed near-doubling worth flagging prominently as one of the most significant single-figure changes in this entire multi-country dataset. Genuinely THREE distinct regimes modeled here (Irish-citizen sponsor with the new €75,000 test, EU Treaty Rights with no income test, and Category C non-EEA with a qualifying-period-plus-income-test structure) — each carries materially different requirements, consistent with how this dataset's schema is designed to capture route variation via groups rather than fragmenting into separate files. International-protection beneficiaries now face a NEW 2-year wait before family reunification (effective the same 12 June 2026 reform) — not modeled as a fourth group here given scope, but flagged as a real, additional tightening layered onto the same reform date.
